domain.value: self-supervised video encoder trained by FEATURE PREDICTION in latent space (x-encoder + predictor regress EMA target-encoder features of masked spatio-temporal regions with an L1 loss); no pixel decoder; described by its authors as non-generative. Trained on general video (VideoMix2M).
authors_wording_generative_vs_not: Meta blog: 'V-JEPA is a non-generative model that learns by predicting missing or masked parts of a video in an abstract representation space.'
Meta blog: 'Unlike generative approaches that try to fill in every missing pixel, V-JEPA has the flexibility to discard unpredictable information'
GitHub README: 'As opposed to generative methods that have a pixel decoder, V-JEPA has a predictor that makes predictions in latent space.'

GitHub README / paper: pretraining 'does not utilize ... pixel-level reconstruction'; paper abstract: 'trained solely using a feature prediction objective, without the use of pretrained image encoders, text, negative examples, reconstruction, or other sources of supervision.'

Note: the README also reports a separately trained conditional diffusion model used only to visualise the frozen predictor's feature-space predictions as pixels; the V-JEPA encoder/predictor themselves stay frozen and are not generative.

quotes.quote: V-JEPA is a non-generative model that learns by predicting missing or masked parts of a video in an abstract representation space.

Unlike generative approaches that try to fill in every missing pixel, V-JEPA has the flexibility to discard unpredictable information, which leads to improved training and sample efficiency by a factor between 1.5x and 6x.
As opposed to generative methods that have a pixel decoder, V-JEPA has a predictor that makes predictions in latent space.

V-JEPA pretraining is based solely on an unsupervised feature prediction objective, and does not utilize pretrained image encoders, text, negative examples, human annotations, or pixel-level reconstruction.

a collection of vision models trained solely using a feature prediction objective, without the use of pretrained image encoders, text, negative examples, reconstruction, or other sources of supervision.
We train a conditional diffusion model to decode the V-JEPA feature-space predictions to interpretable pixels; the pretrained V-JEPA encoder and predictor networks are kept frozen in this process.
The outputs of the predictor are then regressed to the prediction targets using an L 1 L_{1} loss.

architecture.type: ViT x-encoder on 2x16x16 tubelets + narrow ViT predictor (12 blocks, 384-dim); EMA y-encoder supplies targets; multi-block masking
architecture.representation: frozen encoder output tokens (1024-dim ViT-L, 1280-dim ViT-H), pooled downstream by a learned attentive probe

pretraining_data.summary: VideoMix2M (~2M videos) = HowTo100M (1.22M narrated instructional YouTube videos, WikiHow task categories incl. 'Health') + Kinetics-400/600/700 (K710) + Something-Something-v2, minus validation overlap. Named public datasets.
pretraining_data.form: dataset list (named; HowTo100M is an open-ended YouTube-search-derived set)

quotes.quote: We combine several public datasets to construct an unsupervised video pretraining dataset, which we refer to as VideoMix2M. Specifically, we combine the videos from HowTo100M (HT) ( Miech et al., 2019 ) , Kinetics-400/600/700 (K710) ( Kay et al., 2017 ) , and Something-Something-v2 (SSv2) ( Goyal et al., 2017 ) , and remove any overlap with the validation sets of Kinetics-400/600/700 and Something-Something-v2, resulting in approximately 2 million videos.
V-JEPA models are trained by passively watching video pixels from the VideoMix2M dataset

embedding_dim.value: ViT-L/16: 1024 x (8 x 14 x 14) = 1024 x 1568 tokens per 16-frame 224 clip; ViT-H/16: 1280 x 1568; ViT-H/16-384: 1280 x (8 x 24 x 24) = 1280 x 4608. No fixed pooled vector: the authors pool with a learned attentive probe (pooled dim = embed dim).
embedding_dim.derivation: embed_dim from src/models/vision_transformer.py (vit_large 1024, vit_huge 1280); token grid from 16 frames / tubelet 2 and 224/16 or 384/16
